column21: The lug sole does all the work here. Pull-on, chunky, sturdy enough for a real winter — this is the boot for a woman who wants to stop thinking about her shoes in the morning.

column17: black, black suede, espresso, coffee suede, merlot
column21: Italian leather at this price is the kind of thing I check twice. The 2.4 inch stacked heel is the height you can actually stand in all day, and a round toe is far kinder to a wide foot than anything pointed.
A western bootie is either the best thing in your closet or fancy dress, and the difference is whether the appliqué knows when to stop. This one does — and at Rack prices it is worth the gamble.

column17: black, cyprus tan, spiced pecan, cafe noir, warm nutmeg
column21: A demi block heel is the most useful heel there is — it reads dressy and walks like a flat. The square toe keeps it current without dating it to one particular year.

column17: sunstone sand suede, driftwood tan, pearl blush, olive suede
column21: Slouchy suede that only gets better as it softens. This is a boot with an opinion, so wear it with something plain and let it do the talking.
The link detail is the whole boot — one piece of jewellery, built in, so you don't have to add any. At an inch and a quarter it is the heel you forget you are wearing.

column3: Jade Side Zip Comfort Ankle Boot
column21: Six widths, narrow through triple-wide, which almost nothing else in this category offers. If you have spent years being told your foot is the problem, this is the boot that disagrees.
The splurge. A Chelsea boot lives or dies on whether the elastic panel still holds its shape in year five, and this is the one that does. Three inch stacked heel — real height, no wobble.

column3: Italian Leather & Suede Low Profile Sneaker
column17: black, cognac, birch, garnet, shell pink, electric blue
column21: Italian leather and suede at ninety-four dollars, in six colours including a proper electric blue. Low profile means it sits under a trouser hem instead of fighting it.

column17: warm white/rose gold, black, warm silver, warm taupe
column21: Comes in a true wide, which almost no fashion sneaker does. Naturalizer build the footbed properly — this is the one for a woman who walks all day and refuses to look like she's dressed for the gym.
The retro runner that goes with everything and asks nothing of you. The muted colourways are the trick — they read considered rather than sporty.
A platform buys you height without a heel, and the gold trim is the detail that lets a sneaker go somewhere nice. This is the pair for a woman who wants comfort without giving up on shine.
The clean white leather court sneaker, done by the brand that does it best. It will look right with jeans, with a midi skirt, and under a suit on a Friday.

column17: sea salt/concrete, mosaic green, truffle salt, raincloud
column21: The chunky one, and it is chunky on purpose — it balances a wide-leg trouser the way a delicate shoe never will. Runs large, so take a half size down.
Low, slim, and quietly pretty — a sneaker that doesn't shout. Reformation cut it narrow through the foot, so take your usual size only if you already know narrow suits you.

column17: brushed almond, white, fuchsia spark, avola
column21: A court sneaker with enough polish to wear to an office that permits them. Leather lined, which is why it will still look good after a winter.
The splurge. The web stripe is instantly legible and that is either exactly what you want or exactly what you don't. Runs large — take a half size down.
Cotton canvas, big enough for a laptop and a lunch, and it improves with wear rather than looking tired. The one I'd throw in a car without a second thought.

column17: black, olive, dark brown, dark coffee
column21: It zips, which sounds obvious until you own three open-top totes and everything falls out. Vegan faux suede, so it takes weather better than real suede would.
Water-resistant canvas in the shape that has never gone out of style. This is the bag you monogram and then use for fifteen years.

column17: burnt sienna, coffee bean, faded olive, juniper berry
column21: Handwoven leather, so it has texture doing the work instead of hardware. Holds a laptop, and the burnt sienna is the colour I'd pick if you already own a black bag.

column17: black, cappuccino, stone, olive, chili, forest
column21: Italian pebbled leather, unlined, no hardware, twelve colours. The bag for a woman who wants nothing announcing itself — and it takes a 16 inch laptop without bulging.
Fits most 16 inch laptops and still reads as a handbag rather than a briefcase. Coach leather ages properly — it softens instead of cracking.
Suede, slouchy, and the burgundy is genuinely beautiful in a way photographs undersell. This is a bag with a personality — treat it as the outfit, not the afterthought.
The splurge, and an unapologetic one — coated canvas with the web stripe, which means everyone knows what it is. Buy it because you love it, not as an investment.
Thirty dollars to find out whether a big organic shape suits you. That is the right way to test a statement earring — cheaply, before you commit.
Nickel-safe with a titanium post, which matters more than the design if your ears have ever objected. A clean sculptural drop that works with a collar or a turtleneck.
A shell shape that catches light from across a room without being heavy on the lobe. Gorjana's plating holds up far better than the price suggests.
The big polished gold hoop, which is the single most useful statement earring there is. If a woman owns one pair of these she is dressed for most things.
Gold vermeil over sterling, not plated brass, so it will not turn. Organic pearls mean no two pairs match exactly — which is the point.
Architectural, hand-polished, made in the States. A disc this clean is harder to pull off than a hoop and far more interesting when you do.
Nickel-free, sharply drawn, and the link shape reads as design rather than decoration. These are the earrings for a woman who wants to look deliberate in a meeting.
The splurge. Real stones — rock crystal, mother-of-pearl, prasiolite, blue topaz — on sterling, so the colour is depth rather than paint. Chandeliers this size need hair up and nothing at the neck.
Deliberately short and close through the body, which only works over a high waist. Fifteen dollars is exactly the right price to find out whether that proportion suits you.

column3: Puff Short Sleeve Embroidered Tie V-Neck Blouse
column21: Twenty-eight dollars, sizes to 4X, and the embroidery does enough that nothing else is required. The puff is gentle rather than theatrical — worth knowing if big sleeves usually put you off.

column3: Long Sleeve Scalloped V-Neck Button-Up Blouse
column21: Tonal embroidery and a scalloped edge, which is what separates this from every other white button-up at the price. Cotton, so it washes instead of going to the dry cleaner.
